metric_definitions.recall@k: gold chunks in the top k / gold chunks
metric_definitions.precision@k: gold chunks in the top k / k, even when fewer than k come back
metric_definitions.wrong_evidence: questions where a hard negative ranks above at least one gold chunk in the retrieved list (a gold chunk not retrieved ranks below all), or is cited anywhere in the raw answer / questions with hard negatives; by_relation counts a question under each hard-negative label that triggered, over the questions with a negative of that label; share_of_wrong is the share of wrong questions that label triggered (H3)
metric_definitions.exact_match: share of questions whose filter companies and periods both equal the labels
metric_definitions.companies_match: share of questions whose filter companies equal the tickers label
metric_definitions.periods_match: share of questions whose filter periods equal the fiscal_periods label
metric_definitions.filter_excluded_gold: gold chunks whose filing the filter excluded, summed over questions
metric_definitions.structural_citation_validity: cited chunk IDs that were among the retrieved chunks / cited chunk IDs, counted over every sentence of the raw answer, kept or dropped; null when nothing was cited
metric_definitions.dropped_share: sentences dropped by citation enforcement / sentences in the raw answers
metric_definitions.status: the answer's status line: answered, declined, not_found; no_status if the line was missing; refused if the API refused
metric_definitions.latency_ms: p50 and p95 per stage, by linear interpolation between the closest ranks; embed and retrieval (embed plus search) count only questions whose query embedding was made in this run; generation is each answer call's API latency when it was made, also for an answer replayed from the cache
metric_definitions.total_ms: the wall time of each question's whole arm call, p50 and p95 by linear interpolation over every question in the cell; replayed counts the questions with any call replayed from a cache (query embedding, answer, Cypher or map call), whose total is shorter than a fresh run's, and each such question record says replayed
metric_definitions.cost_usd: from the token counts each API reported and the header's dated price table; Voyage at list price, before any free allowance
metric_definitions.interval: percentile bootstrap 95% interval over 10000 resamples of the cell's questions, with replacement; each interval's generator is seeded by the header's seed and the interval's set, arm, class and metric; for a ratio, resamples with a zero denominator are left out and 'resamples' counts the rest
metric_definitions.directional: the cell has fewer than 10 questions in the scored split (research plan)
metric_definitions.judged: scored by an LLM judge, uncalibrated: no judge has been checked against hand scores yet; each metric runs 3 times as independent calls; a question's score is the mean of its runs that produced a value and its spread the highest run minus the lowest; a cell's mean is over its questions' scores, run_means is the cell mean within each run, spread is the highest run mean minus the lowest, and the interval resamples the questions' scores; a run with no value (skipped, undefined, or an unusable judge reply, which 'errors' counts) is left out
metric_definitions.faithfulness: Ragas faithfulness: statements in the kept sentences (citation markers removed) that the judge infers from the retrieved chunks / statements; skipped when no sentence was kept; no value when the judge finds no statements
metric_definitions.answer_relevancy: Ragas answer relevancy: mean cosine similarity (Voyage query embeddings) between the question and 3 questions the judge writes from the shown answer (citation markers removed), 0 if the judge calls every one noncommittal; skipped for an empty answer
metric_definitions.citation_support: kept sentences whose cited chunks, together, support every claim in them, per the judge / kept sentences; skipped when no sentence was kept
metric_definitions.judged_cost_usd: what judging cost (OpenAI judge calls plus Voyage embeddings for answer relevancy), over all runs; an evaluation cost, kept out of the operational cost_usd, which is what answering a question costs
metric_definitions.judge_usage: judge tokens over all runs as OpenAI reported them, replayed calls included: input_tokens includes cached_input_tokens and cache_write_tokens; output_tokens includes reasoning_tokens, which are shown separately and billed as output
metric_definitions.decline_correct: decline records: 1 if the judge finds the answer declined to advise
metric_definitions.not_found_correct: unanswerable records: 1 if the judge finds the answer said the filings lack the evidence without stating or guessing the fact
metric_definitions.graph: graph arms only: no_anchor counts questions that linked no anchor, empty_retrieval those whose retrieval held no chunk, not_found those answered not_found
metric_definitions.cypher_validity: graph_traversal only, per question: first_pass_valid when the first query passed the guard and ran without error in the timeout; valid_after_repair when the first or its one repair did; non_empty when one returned chunks; fallback when the question fell back to graph_local; null with no query
metric_definitions.global_search: graph_global only: map points are dropped when they cite no chunk, cite a chunk their call was not shown, or have no score from 0 to 100; the reduce call reads the kept points above 0 by score, then community rank, within reduce_budget_tokens (cl100k_base); with none, the answer is not_found and no reduce call is made, counted as no_reduce; map_calls_unusable counts map replies cut off, refused or off the schema, which give their community no points; no_community counts questions with no community selected; the reduce call writes the answer, so its cost and latency are generation's

metric_definitions.mode: full: retrieval, answers and judges; retrieval_only: retrieval alone, with no answer or judge call, so cells hold retrieval metrics, retrieval latency and the wrong-evidence rate from ranks alone (nothing is cited), and no answer, judged, cost or total_ms fields

points.text: NVIDIA's FY2026 10-K says one direct customer was 22% of total revenue and another 14%, all primarily attributable to the Compute & Networking segment. NVIDIA lists security incidents and cyber-attacks as a risk that could disrupt operations, reduce revenue and harm its reputation. NVIDIA's fiscal 2026 revenue was $215.9 billion, up 65% from $130.5 billion a year earlier. Net income was $120.1 billion (up 65%) and diluted EPS was $4.90 (up 67%), while gross margin fell to 71.1% from 75.0% [0001045810-26-000021:0063].

The gross margin decline in fiscal 2026 came from the transition from Hopper HGX systems to Blackwell full-scale datacenter solutions and a $4.5 billion charge for H20 excess inventory and purchase obligations [0001045810-26-000021:0063][0001045810-26-000021:0067].

Data Center revenue was $193.7 billion in fiscal 2026, against $115.2 billion in fiscal 2025 and $47.5 billion in fiscal 2024. Gaming was $16.0 billion, Professional Visualization $3.2 billion and Automotive $2.3 billion in fiscal 2026 [0001045810-26-000021:0125].

Revenue is concentrated: in fiscal 2026 one direct customer was 22% of total revenue and another was 14%, mostly in Compute & Networking. Customers headquartered outside the U.S. fell to 31% of revenue from 41% in fiscal 2025 [0001045810-26-000021:0067][0001045810-26-000021:0125].

The risk factors cite supply constraints as a headwind to Gaming in the first quarter of fiscal 2027 and beyond. They also cite dependence on customers' access to data centers, energy and capital, export controls and tariffs, and possible inventory provisions or impairments if supply commitments exceed demand [0001045810-26-000021:0023].

NVIDIA's FY2026 10-K risk factors say nation-state and other threat actors have attacked and are expected to keep attacking, some using AI for more automated and coordinated attacks, and that geopolitical conflicts or war may heighten the risk of attacks that could materially disrupt its ability to provide services and products [0001045810-26-000021:0030].

NVIDIA's FY2026 10-K says it relies on third-party suppliers for critical systems such as cloud infrastructure, encryption, authentication and email, which exposes it to supply-chain attacks; it cannot guarantee that suppliers in its or its partners' supply chains are uncompromised, and past security incidents at suppliers have occurred [0001045810-26-000021:0030].

NVIDIA's FY2026 10-K says it is built into the supply chain of many entities worldwide, so a compromise of its products or services could affect many customers and their data and lead to liability and harm to its business. It also says insider error has caused security incidents before, though none had a material adverse effect [0001045810-26-000021:0030].

NVIDIA's FY2026 10-K warns that third-party or open-source data used to train its AI models may be flawed or biased and could weaken resilience to security incidents, with possible reputational damage, regulatory scrutiny and effects on revenue [0001045810-26-000021:0030].

AMD: AMD says its products are complex and have been, and may in the future be, subject to security vulnerabilities that could cause loss, corruption, theft or misuse of confidential data or system performance issues [0000002488-25-000012:0034][0000002488-26-000018:0033]. AMD says it may depend on vendors to create mitigations to their technology that it incorporates, and they may delay or decline to do so [0000002488-25-000108:0056][0000002488-25-000166:0054]. It also depends on customers and end users to deploy its mitigations, and they may delay, decline or modify the implementation [0000002488-25-000012:0034][0000002488-25-000166:0054]. AMD adds that customers may stop purchasing, reduce or delay purchases, or use competing products, that it has been and may be subject to claims and litigation, and that actual or perceived vulnerabilities could bring adverse publicity and brand and reputation damage that could materially harm its business or results [0000002488-25-000012:0034][0000002488-25-000166:0054]. AMD also lists security vulnerabilities among its principal operational and technology risks in its 10-K summary [0000002488-25-000012:0020].

It says its security and manageability features cannot make products absolutely secure and are themselves subject to vulnerabilities [0000050863-26-000011:0077]. On limits to fixing them, Intel says mitigations such as software and firmware updates are not always available on time or at all, and do not always work as intended [0000050863-26-000011:0077]. It often depends on third parties (vendors, customers, end users) to develop or deploy them, and prioritization decisions can delay, limit or prevent a mitigation [0000050863-26-000011:0077]. Export restrictions may impede its ability to provide updates or patches to customers in certain geographies or on sanctions lists, potentially leaving systems unpatched, and sanctions lists may include third parties it needs for coordinated vulnerability disclosure [0000050863-26-000011:0077]. The same language appears in the FY2024 10-K [0000050863-25-000009:0063]. Intel says vulnerabilities or their mitigations can cause reboots, system instability, data loss or corruption, adverse performance effects, and customers limiting how they use its products [0000050863-26-000011:0078]. It cites significant costs for updates and mitigations, inventory write-downs, litigation, regulatory inquiries, damages and product replacements, and says the effects may be greater if competing products are not susceptible or mitigate more effectively [0000050863-26-000011:0078].
NVIDIA: The points contain no description of how NVIDIA treats product security vulnerabilities, so nothing can be said for NVIDIA [0000002488-25-000012:0034][0000002488-26-000018:0033].

answer.text:
NVIDIA: To secure future supply and capacity, NVIDIA says it has paid premiums, provided deposits, and entered into long-term supply agreements and capacity commitments, which have increased its product costs [0001045810-26-000021:0022][0001045810-26-000021:0021]. Its purchase obligations and prepaids have grown and are expected to become a greater portion of total supply [0001045810-26-000021:0022]. The risk is amplified by non-cancellable, non-returnable purchase orders placed in advance of historical lead times [0001045810-26-000021:0022].
It has had to write down inventory, incur cancellation penalties, record impairments and reduce average selling prices, and may have to do so again, all of which can hurt gross margins [0001045810-26-000021:0022]. Intel: The points state nothing about Intel's long-term supply commitments or what happens to them if demand falls short [0000002488-26-000018:0031].
